---
title: "Visitation Shifts After 2020"
subtitle: "Category recovery trajectories and the individual park units with the largest post-2019 shifts"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
toc: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup-story-combined
library(tidyverse)
library(htmltools)

annual_visits <- read_csv(
  "nps_annual_visits_1979_2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    suffix = word(park, -1),
    park_type = case_when(
      suffix %in% c("NP", "NPRES", "PRES") ~ "National Parks & Preserves",
      suffix %in% c("NRA", "NS", "NL", "PKWY", "NR", "NSR", "W&SR", "NRRA") ~ "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
      suffix %in% c("NM", "Monument") ~ "National Monuments",
      TRUE ~ "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials"
    ),
    park_type = factor(
      park_type,
      levels = c(
        "National Parks & Preserves",
        "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
        "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials",
        "National Monuments"
      )
    )
  )

# 1. Balanced panel for category recovery index (2015-2025)
balanced_index <- annual_visits |>
  filter(year >= 2015) |>
  group_by(park) |>
  filter(n() == 11) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(park_type, year) |>
  summarize(total_visits = sum(recreation_visits), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(park_type) |>
  mutate(
    index_2019 = 100 * total_visits / total_visits[year == 2019]
  ) |>
  ungroup()

end_labels <- balanced_index |>
  filter(year == 2025) |>
  mutate(
    label_y = case_when(
      park_type == "National Parks & Preserves" ~ index_2019 + 1.6,
      park_type == "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways" ~ index_2019 - 1.6,
      park_type == "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials" ~ index_2019 + 1.8,
      park_type == "National Monuments" ~ index_2019 - 1.8
    ),
    label_text = sprintf("%.1f", index_2019)
  )

palette_cols <- c(
  "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways" = "#4A7C82",
  "National Parks & Preserves" = "#2F6B48",
  "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials" = "#C48347",
  "National Monuments" = "#A45D57"
)

# 2. Individual park shift data (2019 vs 2025)
change_data <- annual_visits |>
  filter(year %in% c(2019, 2025)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = recreation_visits,
    names_prefix = "year_"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(year_2019), !is.na(year_2025)) |>
  mutate(
    absolute_change = year_2025 - year_2019,
    percent_change = 100 * absolute_change / year_2019
  )

rising <- change_data |>
  slice_max(absolute_change, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(group = "Largest increases (+)")

falling <- change_data |>
  slice_min(absolute_change, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(group = "Largest decreases (-)")

change_sample <- bind_rows(rising, falling) |>
  mutate(
    park = forcats::fct_reorder(park, absolute_change),
    label_text = ifelse(
      absolute_change > 0,
      paste0("+", scales::label_comma(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(absolute_change)),
      scales::label_comma(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(absolute_change)
    ),
    label_hjust = ifelse(absolute_change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)
  )

```

The 2020 pandemic triggered sharp, uneven disruptions across the National Park System. Open outdoor destinations like scenic parkways and flagship national parks rebounded quickly—surpassing pre-pandemic benchmarks by 2025. In contrast, urban monuments and historic sites took deeper hits and still trail 2019 attendance by roughly 14%. Below, trace the category-wide recovery trajectories followed by the individual park units with the largest post-2019 volume shifts.

## Category Recovery Trajectories (2015–2025)

```{r}
#| label: fig-balanced-divergence
#| fig-cap: "Annual recreation visits across 372 continuously reporting NPS units, summed by category and indexed so each category's 2019 total equals 100."
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot(balanced_index, aes(x = year, y = index_2019, color = park_type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "#667085", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2020, linetype = "dotted", color = "#8C4A58", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  geom_label(
    data = end_labels,
    aes(x = 2025.14, y = label_y, label = label_text),
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = "#FAF7F0",
    label.size = 0,
    label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2015:2025,
    limits = c(2015, 2025.85)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(38, 114),
    breaks = seq(40, 110, by = 10)
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 2018.85,
    y = 103.5,
    label = "2019 baseline = 100",
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3.2,
    color = "#4A5B51",
    fill = "#FAF7F0",
    label.size = 0
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2020.12,
    y = 40.5,
    label = "2020 drop",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "italic",
    color = "#7A2E3A"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Parks & Parkways Passed 2019 While Monuments & Historic Sites Trailed",
    subtitle = "Annual visits across 372 continuously reporting units, indexed to 2019 total (= 100)",
    x = "Calendar Year",
    y = "Visitation index (2019 = 100)",
    color = "Park Unit Category",
    caption = "Source: NPS Visitor Use Statistics (2015–2025 balanced panel)."
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1E382B", size = 14.2),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#4A5B51"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#5A6B60", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## 2019 to 2025: Largest Park Shifts

```{r}
#| label: fig-rising-falling
#| fig-cap: "Top 10 absolute increases and decreases in annual recreation visits between 2019 and 2025 among units reporting in both years."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8.2

ggplot(change_sample, aes(x = absolute_change, y = park, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#1E382B", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label_text, hjust = label_hjust),
    size = 3.6,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1E382B"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Largest increases (+)" = "#2F6B48",
      "Largest decreases (-)" = "#B06242"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
    limits = c(-3350000, 2750000),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Net change in annual recreation visits (2019 to 2025)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: NPS Visitor Use Statistics. Units reporting in both 2019 and 2025."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#E6E1D2", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#1E382B"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "#1E382B"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "#4A5B51", size = 10.5)
  )
```
